senses.gloss: f. (תָּרָה Hif.) making one acquainted with the law on a certain subject, esp. the legal warning, by witnesses, given to the offender immediately before committing the offense.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 8b:6">Snh. 8ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>חבר אינו צריך ה׳ וכ׳</he> a student requires no warning, for the law requiring warning is intended only to enable the court to decide between the willful and the ignorant offender.

<cite ref="Shevuot 3b:8">Shebu. 3ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הַתְרָאַת ספק</he> a warning under doubt, e.g. one swears that he will do a certain thing during this day, when the actual moment of the offense (of omission) cannot be defined, so as to make the warning precede it, immediately.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:4:9">Y. Pes. V, 32ᶜ</cite> top <he>מקבלין התרייה על ספק</he> warning is accepted (considered legal) on a doubtful offense; a. fr.—Pl. <he>הַתְרָיוֹת</he>, <he>הַתְרָאוֹת</he>. Y. B. Kam. VII, 5ᵈ bot.; a. e.
